note: Toll rose steadily: 2 (15 Aug, CGTN) → 14 → 38 → 47 → 51 (16 Aug) → 54 (17 Aug) → 68 (17–18 Aug) → 70 (18–19 Aug) → 73 (19 Aug) → 75 (20 Aug) → 83 (21 Aug) → 87 (22 Aug, BNPB via Detik/Wikipedia citation) as rescue teams reached remote villages. Injured count climbed to 1,298 (336 seriously) by 22 August, up from the reconciled 986 figure reported 21 August.

BNPB spokesman confirmed the 8 deaths added between 20-21 August were from indirect earthquake impacts (aftershock-triggered shock, falls) rather than structural collapse: Manggarai 2, East Manggarai 2, Nagekeo 3, Ngada 1.
A resident died of a heart attack/shock triggered by a magnitude 5.8 aftershock at 06:45 WITA on 20 August in Ruteng; additive to the mainshock total.

Mateus Noba Noba (74), Waiula Village, Wulanggitang District, died 15 August fleeing his home during the mainshock; the death was not reported to provincial disaster officials until 20 August because Flores Timur Regency never declared an emergency-response status, leaving it outside BNPB's official tally.
Aftershock-specific deaths, additive to the mainshock total.
Highest single-regency death toll; figure not yet broken down by injured count.
Second-highest single-regency death toll, adjacent to Manggarai Regency.
Reported as an aggregate figure across four regencies rather than broken out individually.

As of 18–19 Aug, local officials reported no further outstanding reports of people trapped or missing beneath rubble, though NGOs caution that 812 disabled cell sites may mask undercounting in cut-off hamlets.
Includes 15 patients + 5 infants treated in tents at Ende Regional Hospital and surgical patients evacuated after Ruteng's operating theatre was destroyed.
986 tourists evacuated to Labuan Bajo; no injuries reported among the tourist population.
